questions.question: What does @RequestBody do in a Spring MVC controller method?
options: It reads the request body and converts it into a Java object
It reads a value from the query string
It marks the method as returning a view name
It sets the status code of the response
questions.explanation: @RequestBody tells Spring to deserialize the HTTP request body, usually JSON, into the method parameter.

questions.question: Which header must a client send so that Spring reads the body as JSON?
questions.explanation: Content-Type tells the server the format of the body, and Spring picks the JSON converter from it.

questions.question: A record Ping(String name, int count) is the @RequestBody type. The client posts {"count":3} as JSON. What does name hold?
questions.explanation: A key that is missing from the JSON leaves the field as null. Spring does not check that fields are present.

questions.question: A client sends POST with Content-Type text/plain and a body of hello to a method that expects a record through @RequestBody. What status does it get?
questions.explanation: No converter can turn text/plain into the record, so Spring answers 415 Unsupported Media Type.

questions.question: A method is declared as create(@RequestBody Order order, @RequestBody Payment payment). What is wrong?
options: Records cannot be used as request types
A request has only one body, so the method should take one @RequestBody object that holds both parts
@RequestBody must be placed on the class
questions.explanation: The body can be read only once, so wrap the order and payment in one class and use a single @RequestBody.
